verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Rainfall in each plot's season was the highest on record, roughly double the year before, and every plot stood in the open, watered by rain alone." Record double rainfall on rain-only open plots explains the 8-13 cm gains against the previous summer just as well as the fertilizer does.

Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the kit was issued: case one was "issued 4 November; by 27 September" and case three was "issued 5 June; by 28 April." Completion gains dated ahead of the intervention cannot have been caused by it.

The outcome is measured on a self-selected subset: "Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route, and about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route." The excluded sixth is exactly the set most likely to have run long, and it is compared against "the same runs a month earlier," i.e. the full unfiltered population.

The absence figures cover a filtered subgroup, not the cohort: "Absence figures cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable." A fifth of each cohort is dropped on a post-switch criterion, yet the comparison is to "the same cohort a term earlier" in full.
